newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Dhaka aims for foodgrains output of 25 mln tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Dhaka aims for foodgrains output of 25 mln tonnes.

text.p: Bangladesh said on Wednesday it was aiming to increase its production of foodgrain by some 25 percent to 25 million tonnes by 2000.

"We need to eradicate hunger and malnutrition to build Bangladesh as a robust and healthy nation," Food and Agriculture Minister Begum Matia Chowdhury told a senimar to mark the World Food Day on Wednesday.

"Malnutrition is seriously affecting the physical and mental growth of children," the official BSS news agency quoted her as saying. She called for improvements in every sector of agriculture, including poultry and fish breeding.

Agriculture officials told the seminar, jointly organised with the U.N. Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO), that a multi-disciplinary task force was already working on plans to increase food production by five million tonnes over the next four years.

At present Bangladesh, with a population of some 120 million, produces about 20 million tonnes of foodgrain annually, officials said. It imports up to three million tonnes to make up for shortfalls and ensure adequate reserves.

Agriculture experts said Bangladesh would have to conduct vigorous research to produce higher yielding varieties of rice and use more environmentally friendly fertilisers if it wanted to raise harvests without damaging soil fertility.
Professor Harun Yusuf of Dhaka University warned that 85 percent of soil in Bangladesh "is in a critical state" due to the widespread use of chemical fertilisers.
"Chemical fertilisers are severely reducing soil fertlity," he told the seminar.
